title: Making precision breeding bloom: APL is a promising target to engineer flowering time
content: Building a perfect plant that possesses all the desirable traits in a specific environment is the core of plant breeding. Precision breeding involves using gene editing, with tools such as CRISPR/Cas9, base-editing, or other site-directed nucleases to precisely modify specific DNA targets to produce a desired effect (Kamburova et al. 2017). Precision breeding touts the ability to speed up the development of new cultivars and make improvements in species with low genetic diversity and long-lived species, such as trees (Sheridan 2025). With the invention and improvement of gene editing technologies, regulatory approval of their use, and identification of gene targets for specific trait improvement, we are one step closer to the ability to pick and choose which traits we want a plant to have.
